title: Son of Adam (Luke 3:23–38)
hookLine: Luke's family tree goes back to Adam, son of God

cards: Lists of names in the Bible are easy to skim. But look where Luke puts his. Jesus has just been baptized in the Jordan.
The heavens open, the Holy Ghost comes down in bodily shape like a dove, and a voice from heaven says: thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.
And right there, before Jesus says a word in public, Luke stops the story for a family tree. Where he puts it matters, and where it ends matters more.

teach.h: AS IT WAS SUPPOSED, SON OF JOSEPH.
teach.b: It starts, in the Douay-Rheims: "And Jesus himself was beginning about the age of thirty years; being (as it was supposed) the son of Joseph." As it was supposed.

Luke has already told us about the angel and Mary, and he doesn't let us forget it, even here. Then the list runs backward, father by father: Heli, Matthat, a long run of names, then David, Jesse, Judah, Isaac, Abraham.

And it keeps going, past Abraham, past Noah, to the last line: "Who was of Henos, who was of Seth, who was of Adam, who was of God." Matthew's family tree runs forward and starts with Abraham, the father of Israel.
Luke's runs backward, all the way to Adam.
And adam, in Hebrew, is also the ordinary word for a human being; Genesis sets it beside adamah, the ground he was formed from.
Christians read Luke's list as saying that this beloved Son belongs not only to one people, but to the whole human family.
An honest note: between David and Joseph, Matthew and Luke give mostly different names, and the Gospels never explain why.

Christian writers have proposed answers: that one list traces Joseph's line and the other Mary's, or, from an early writer named Julius Africanus, that a custom of marrying a brother's widow gave Joseph both a natural and a legal father.
The Church hasn't settled on one.

teach.h: WHO WAS OF ADAM, WHO WAS OF GOD.
teach.b: Either way, Luke's list ends where he wants you to look: son of Adam, son of God.

how: At every Mass the Universal Prayer, or prayers of the faithful, asks God's help for the Church, the world, and all people in need, the whole human family.

games.q: you're Luke. a voice from heaven has just called Jesus my beloved Son. where do you take his family tree?
o: back to Abraham, father of Israel, and stop.
back past Abraham, all the way to Adam, who was of God.
nowhere; you skip the family tree.
games.why: Luke goes all the way back: who was of Adam, who was of God. a son for the whole human family.

practice: Start with the people closest to you and hold them for a breath; then widen to your street, your town, the people you passed today without noticing; then wider still, to strangers, people who speak languages you don't know, people you find hard to love.
Luke's list runs back to one father, Adam, for all of them. If you pray, pray for them together, the whole human family; if not, let the circle stay that wide for a minute.

wordCard.voice: adam. Hebrew for a human being: the name Luke's family tree for Jesus runs back to, past Abraham, tying him to the whole human family. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Adam, a human being, related to adamah, the ground he was formed from.

carryVoice: Your line: everyone's family. Every branch runs back to the same ground. Four hundred fifty days now.
